inventoryMethod: Bounded source-first review of the upstream package manifest, public feature and API documentation, TypeScript declarations, and focused HTTP/XHR/fetch dispatch implementation. The review covered 28 upstream paths, did not execute target code or tests, and treated examples as documented patterns rather than runtime proof.

items.userNeed: Call HTTP APIs from JavaScript in browser and server applications and receive a Promise-based response.
items.summary: Axios exposes a callable client and method aliases for GET, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, POST, PUT, PATCH and form variants; requests resolve to an Axios response or reject with an Axios error.
qualifiers: The reviewed package version is 1.19.0.
Actual protocol behavior depends on the selected adapter and runtime.
No target code or endpoint was executed in this experiment.

items.userNeed: Reuse service-specific base URLs, headers, timeouts and other defaults while retaining per-request overrides.
items.summary: axios.create() creates isolated preconfigured instances using the full request config; request-time values override instance defaults, and instance defaults remain mutable.
qualifiers: baseURL is URL-construction convenience, not a path or origin security boundary.
The only generally required request config field is url; method defaults to GET.

items.userNeed: Send query parameters and common request body formats, then transform request and response data.
items.summary: Axios supports custom query serialization, request/response transforms, JSON, URL-encoded and multipart/FormData payloads, including automatic object-to-FormData serialization.
qualifiers: Accepted body types vary across browser, React Native and Node.js environments.
Browser, web worker and React Native FormData must leave multipart Content-Type boundary generation to the runtime.
Node.js FormData getHeaders() defaults to legacy all-header copying; content-only is the stricter opt-in policy.
The default form serializer nesting limit is documented as 100.

items.userNeed: Authenticate API calls and control browser credential and XSRF-token transmission.
items.summary: Axios can send explicit headers, HTTP Basic credentials, URL-derived Basic credentials in Node HTTP/fetch adapters, cross-site credentials, and browser XSRF headers under configurable same-origin or cross-origin conditions.
qualifiers: The auth option is HTTP Basic only and overwrites a custom Authorization header; Bearer tokens and API keys use custom headers or query parameters.
withCredentials and withXSRFToken control different browser behaviors.
Credentials and tokens are outbound request data disclosed to the configured destination; no retention behavior is established.

items.userNeed: Apply shared request and response policy such as header injection, logging, refresh or response shaping.
items.summary: Request and response interceptors can modify or reject config and responses, can be isolated per instance, conditionally run, ejected or cleared, and have documented LIFO request versus FIFO response ordering.
qualifiers: Request interceptors are asynchronous by default unless marked synchronous.
Retry and token-refresh examples are application-authored interceptor policies, not an Axios built-in retry or credential lifecycle engine.

items.userNeed: Stop obsolete or stalled requests and bound request or response resource use.
items.summary: Axios accepts AbortSignal cancellation and timeout configuration; legacy CancelToken remains available but deprecated. Node HTTP/fetch adapters expose request/response size caps, while decompression-bomb protection is opt-in because default limits are unlimited.
qualifiers: CancelToken is deprecated in favor of AbortController.
Timeout error code defaults to ECONNABORTED unless clarifyTimeoutError is enabled.
maxContentLength and maxBodyLength enforcement is adapter-dependent and defaults to -1.

items.userNeed: Consume response data, status and headers and distinguish HTTP, network, timeout, cancellation and setup failures.
items.summary: The response contains data, status, statusText, normalized headers, config and the underlying request. AxiosError exposes config, code, status and optional response/request context; validateStatus changes resolve/reject policy and redact masks selected fields only during error serialization.
qualifiers: The default success policy resolves 2xx and rejects other statuses.
Browser security policies may prevent Axios from distinguishing CORS or mixed-content failures from generic network errors.
redact does not alter transmitted request data or the original config.

items.userNeed: Report upload/download progress and limit bandwidth for large transfers.
items.summary: Axios emits throttled upload and download progress with byte, rate and estimate information in browser and Node contexts; the Node HTTP adapter can cap upload and download bytes per second.
qualifiers: Progress events are limited to three per second.
Node.js FormData upload progress is not currently supported.
Node.js streaming uploads should disable redirects to avoid documented whole-stream buffering.
maxRate has no effect in browser environments and is limited to the Node.js HTTP adapter.

items.userNeed: Use one client API across browser, Node.js and fetch-based runtimes or substitute a custom transport.
items.summary: Axios selects among xhr, http and fetch adapters by environment, accepts explicit priority or a custom adapter, and offers experimental HTTP/2 through the Node.js HTTP adapter.
qualifiers: Adapter feature support is not uniform across runtimes.
HTTP/2 is Node.js-only, experimental, and does not automatically follow redirects.
A custom adapter owns request execution and must return an Axios-shaped response.

items.userNeed: Understand whether retries, backoff and caching are built in or must be supplied by the application.
items.summary: The reviewed retry guide implements retry, backoff, 429 handling and opt-out flags in application response interceptors; it does not present these as an automatic Axios retry engine.
qualifiers: Retrying non-idempotent mutations can duplicate remote effects and must be an application policy decision.
No built-in cache policy was established from the bounded public docs, declarations and focused implementation reviewed; cache behavior remains unknown rather than asserted absent.

limitations: This is a bounded discovery inventory, not an exhaustive API catalog, gold standard, runtime conformance result or security audit.
No target source, tests, builds, examples, endpoints or external links were executed.
Public docs were treated as claims and cross-checked against declarations or focused implementation for request dispatch, adapter configuration and data-flow details where practical.
Proxy, redirect, Unix socket, decompression codec, detailed header API and every exported helper were not independently inventoried as separate consumer outcomes.
Server-side storage, logging, retention and downstream use of transmitted request data are outside Axios and were not established.
Caching behavior was not established within the bounded source review.
